issues.description: Template method name does not match the method called in the class run() and the method implemented in the solution. In template/ex1_grover_two_qubit_without_auxiliary_qubit.py the Grover builder method is declared as build_grover(...), but run() calls self.grover_circuit(...). The problem statement and solution use the name grover_circuit. This name mismatch prevents student code from running as-is and is likely to confuse students about the expected method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method build_grover(...) to grover_circuit(...) to match the run() call and the problem statement (or change run() to call build_grover). Ensure the method signature and docstring align with the expected grover_circuit(...) name used in tests and the solution so students have a consistent API to implement.

issues.description: The template and solution use different method names for the same conceptual operation of assembling the one-iteration Grover circuit. In the template the method stub is named build_grover, while the solution (and the template's run() caller) expects grover_circuit. This mismatch creates confusion for students (and causes the template's run() to call a nonexistent method), making it unclear which method they should implement to satisfy the exercise and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across template and solution. Rename the template stub build_grover to grover_circuit (or change run() to call build_grover) so the method name matches the expected grover_circuit used by the solution and tests. Update any references/comments accordingly to avoid ambiguity.
